In this case, we have to use the identity $1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x.$ Rearranging this gives

$$
{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1.
$$

Using the above, we compute the given integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}4({sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =4{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}1\,\text{d}x \\  & =4x\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =4(\frac{\pi }{4}-0) \\  & =\pi \end{aligned}
$$
